item.title: Can Democrats stop Iran war, reverse Trump’s tariffs after midterms win?
item.description:
SHREVEPORT, La. — The GOP's election-night defeat has unleashed a wave of finger-pointing inside the House Republican conference, with members questioning whether Speaker Mike Johnson or any of the other top deputies can survive next week's leadership elections. Why it matters: Johnson spent months insisting Republicans would defy the odds and keep the House. But after losing the majority, he cast the defeat as all but inevitable, an explanation unlikely to satisfy Republicans ready for a new leadership slate. One House Republican told Axios that every member of GOP leadership will face a challenger because of the election results. Another said the losses have created a major opening for Republicans looking to challenge the current leadership team. item.title: Blue wave sweeps across America: 'In 1974, we had Watergate babies, now we have Iran War babies'
item.description:

But the opposition pulls its punches and is unable to assert Congress' check on the president. The year is 2026. Democrats have swept the midterm congressional elections after a Republican administration launched an unpopular war in a Middle Eastern country. What will happen next? item.title: These trans and nonbinary candidates just made history
item.description:
Six transgender and nonbinary candidates made history on Election Day by winning races in states that have never elected a trans person into their legislature before. These candidates will expand LGBTQ+ political power at a time when their rights are increasingly under attack nationwide. All races are called according to projections by Decision Desk HQ. Georgia Bentley Hudgins will be Georgia’s first nonbinary and first Japanese-American lawmaker after winning their bid to represent State House District 90 in east Atlanta. They easily defeated their opponent, Republican Samantha Boston, in the deep-blue district. Hudgins, a 33-year-old democratic socialist, spent the last three years advocating for LGBTQ+ rights in the Georgia statehouse through their work with the Human Rights Campaign. item.title: US midterms: Trump reacts to the Democrats’ sweeping victory
item.description:
Stock and bond markets gained following Democrats’ midterm victories on buoyant hopes for the US economy and fiscal picture, but some tech stocks declined on concerns over an expected slowdown in the AI infrastructure buildout. Though the results mean control of the government will be divided, markets “ like gridlock — they don’t like a party with too much power,” a Morgan Stanley executive told CNBC. Bets that US borrowing will slow helped bolster US Treasurys, while another investor told Bloomberg that “ the fundamental backdrop has not suddenly changed , with US growth remaining solid.” Some companies slipped, though: Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Tesla both fell ; the GOP supporter spent heavily, and unsuccessfully, to defeat Democrats in Texas, where both firms are based. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Gina Hinojosa pulls off stunning upset to become Texas’ first Latina governor
item.description:
Nevada Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford has successfully ousted Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo in Nevada, a significant pickup for Democrats in the critical battleground state, The Associated Press projects. Ford's defeat of Lombardo comes in one of the most closely watched gubernatorial races in the country. Ford’s victory makes him Nevada’s first Black governor and gives Democrats control of the governor’s office for the first time since Lombardo defeated Democratic Gov. Steve Sisolak in 2022. Ford, who has served as Nevada’s attorney general since 2019, campaigned on affordability, housing, education, healthcare and protecting access to abortion. He argued that Nevada families were struggling with high housing costs, energy bills and other rising expenses under Lombardo and the Republican administration. Brian Poindexter, Democratic congressional candidate for Ohio, during a campaign event at UAW 1250 in Brook Park, Ohio, on Nov. 1, 2026. —Dustin Franz—Bloomberg/Getty Images Democrat Brian Poindexter, a union worker and local councilman, has beaten out Republican Rep.
